definition: Cured-in-place pipe is a rehabilitation method that forms a hardened lining inside an existing pipe instead of excavating its entire length.
entry_text: Cured-in-place pipe is a rehabilitation method that forms a hardened lining inside an existing pipe instead of excavating its entire length.
example: A utility renews a deteriorated sewer segment from existing access points.
label: Cured-in-place pipe
